content: DEFB126, also known as Beta-defensin 126, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the DEFB126 gene. Defensins are polypeptides that are rich in cysteine residues and carry a positive charge (cationic). These molecules play a critical role in the immune system's defense against invading microorganisms. The protein encoded by the DEFB126 gene is secreted and belongs to the beta-defensin family of proteins. Beta-defensin genes are distributed in several clusters throughout the human genome. Specifically, the DEFB126 gene is located in a cluster on chromosome 20 at position 20p13.2. This gene has also been studied in cynomolgus monkeys. Research has indicated that a common genetic variation in the DEFB126 gene can lead to the production of abnormal mRNA. This abnormality may result in a partial impairment of fertility.
